title: Harnessing the Bioorthogonal Inverse Electron Demand Diels-Alder Cycloaddition for Pretargeted PET Imaging
protocol: Dissolve 7 mg NH2-Bn-NOTA in 600 µl NaHCO3 buffer (0.1 M, pH 8.1).
Check the pH of the NH2-Bn-NOTA solution and adjust to 8.1 if necessary using small aliquots of 0.1 M Na2CO3.
Add the NH2-Bn-NOTA solution to 0.5 mg Tz-NHS in a microcentrifuge tube.
Allow the reaction mixture to react for 30 min at room temperature with mild agitation.
Purify the product using reversed-phase C18 HPLC chromatography to remove unreacted NH2-Bn-NOTA.
Monitor the NH2-Bn-NOTA at a wavelength of 254 nm and Tz-NHS, Tz-Bn-NOTA at 525 nm during purification.
Prepare a 1 mg/ml (2.7 mM) solution of TCO-NHS in dry DMF.
Prepare a 2 mg/ml (13.3 μM) solution of huA33 in 1 ml of phosphate buffered saline, pH 7.4.
Adjust the pH of the antibody solution to 8.8-9.0 using small aliquots of 0.1 M Na2CO3.
Monitor the pH with either pH paper or a pH meter with a microelectrode.
Add a volume of TCO-NHS solution corresponding to 8 molar equivalents of activated ester.
Gently mix the solution by inverting the microcentrifuge tube several times.
Wrap the microcentrifuge tube in opaque aluminum foil.
Incubate the solution for 1 hr at RT with mild agitation.
Rinse the size exclusion column as described by the supplier to remove preservatives.
Add the reaction mixture to the size exclusion column.
Rinse the column with 1.5 ml of 0.9% sterile saline.
Collect the product using 2 ml of 0.9% sterile saline as eluent.
Measure the concentration of the resultant huA33-TCO on a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Concentrate the huA33-TCO solution using a centrifugal filter unit with a 50,000 molecular weight cut-off if a higher concentration is desired.
Store the completed huA33-TCO immunoconjugate at 4°C in the dark.
Prepare a 0.5 mg/ml (723 µM) solution of Tz-Bn-NOTA in a 1.7 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add 10 μl of the Tz-Bn-NOTA solution (5 μg) to 400 μl of 0.2 M NH4OAc pH 5.5 buffer in a 1.7 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Measure and record the amount of radioactivity in the sample before the protocol steps.
Add 2,000 µCi (74 MBq) of 64Cu to the Tz-Bn-NOTA solution.
Incubate the solution for 10 min at RT with mild agitation.
Purify the product using reversed-phase C18 HPLC chromatography.
Remove the HPLC eluent using a rotary evaporator.
Redissolve the 64Cu-Tz-Bn-NOTA product in 0.9% sterile saline.
Subcutaneously implant 1 x 10^6 SW1222 colorectal cancer cells into a female athymic nude mouse.
Allow the implanted cells to grow into a 100-150 mm^3 xenograft (9-12 days after inoculation).
Dilute an aliquot of the huA33-TCO solution to a concentration of 0.5 mg/ml in 0.9% sterile saline.
Inject 200 µl of the diluted huA33-TCO solution (100 µg) into the tail vein of the xenograft-bearing mouse.
Allow 24 hours for the accumulation of the huA33-TCO in the tumor.
Dilute the 64Cu-Tz-Bn-NOTA radioligand to a concentration of 1.5 mCi/ml in 0.9% sterile saline.
Inject 200 µl of the diluted 64Cu-Tz-Bn-NOTA solution (300 µCi; 11.1 MBq; 1.6 nmol) into the tail vein of the xenograft-bearing mouse.
At the desired imaging time point (e.g., 2, 6, 12, or 24 hr post-injection), anesthetize the mouse with a 2% isoflurane:oxygen gas mixture.
Place the mouse on the bed of the small animal PET scanner.
Verify anesthesia using the toe-pinch method.
Apply veterinary ointment to the eyes of the mouse to prevent drying during anesthesia.
Maintain anesthesia during the scan using a 1% isoflurane:oxygen gas mixture.
Acquire the PET data for the mouse via a static scan with a minimum of 20 million coincident events using an energy window of 350-700 keV and a coincidence timing window of 6 nsec.
Do not leave the mouse unattended after completing the acquisition of the image.
Do not place the mouse in a cage with other mice until it has regained consciousness.
